scenes.title: Every new story needs healthy volunteers first
scenes.vo: Labs study people who can't respond after brain injury by playing them stories in the scanner. But every new story needs its own 12-15 healthy volunteers scanned first, in that language. For a new story, StillHere gives labs a first reading with zero volunteer scans, measured against each listener's own brain. It has been tested only in healthy volunteers.

items.text: 1 in 4 brain-injured patients who could not follow commands at the bedside showed command-following brain activity on fMRI or EEG (Bodien et al., NEJM 2024).
At university scanner rates ($450-700 an hour), 12-15 volunteers is roughly $5,000-15,000 of scanner time per new story, before recruitment.
Passive tests play a story or a film, and every new one needs healthy volunteers scanned first (Naci et al., PNAS 2014, used a film).
Build a test from this new story, with a scrambled control.
Muse Spark 1.3 plans it: the intact story and a sentence-scrambled control, the only kinds it has evidence for.

scenes.title: Muse Voice Transcribe checks every version

items.text: Muse Voice Transcribe checks every version before anyone is scanned: the intact story kept 99% of its words; the sentence scramble kept 98% of its words in a new order.
The word scramble kept only 16% of its words, so it was caught as broken before scanning and is not used.

scenes.title: How much is the forecast worth?

items.text: On a held-out audiobook, the forecast was worth about 5 real volunteers, and at least 2.
TRIBE v2 forecasts the healthy-adult response. It agreed with the classic sound test.
What it had to beat: word rate and the sound envelope.
Le Petit Prince, section 8, held out: recomputed with code built during the event; first measured Oct 22-23.

items.text: A first healthy reference for a new test, with zero scans, and evidence for how far to trust it.

TRIBE v2 (Meta FAIR, CC BY-NC 4.0) was trained on Courtois NeuroMod, BoldMoments, Lebel2023 and Wen2017 and evaluated by its authors on NNDb, LPP, Narratives and HCP (d'Ascoli et al. 2026, arXiv 2605.04326, Table 1); the film is the one check on data TRIBE's authors never used.
